To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have evaluated the one loop diagrams for Higgs bosons from gluon fusion in mUED, and have evaluated enhancement factors of Higgs production and decay over mUED parameter space, and have derived limits on mUED parameter space from Higgs boson searches at the LHC, and that we have performed a rigorous combination of several HIGGS boson search channels.

we have derived the most stringent limits to date on the parameter space of minimal universal extra dimensions using the most recent Higgs searches from the LHC, and have confirmed previous results on Higgs production and decay in minimal UED.
the Higgs bosons in the minimal universal extra dimension models have a significantly enhanced production and decay rate, and the LHC has excluded a large part of the parameter space.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) at the LHC using the Higgs bosons as probes.
the study of the Higgs bosons in the context of Universal Extra Dimensions (mUED), and in particular the search for the Higgs bosonic signatures at the Large Hadron Collider.
the phenomenology of the Higgs bosons within the context of the Standard Model and its extensions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

mUED has been ruled out for a range of values of R, and that the LHC is now starting to probe the remaining parameter space of mUED, but it will take more data to probe the entire range of values for R.
the mUED scenario is excluded by the Higgs data at 95% confidence level for all values of the parameter space, except for very small values of the compactification radius, $R^{-1} \lesssim 1$~TeV.

the mUED model has been ruled out at the 95% CL by Higgs boson searches at the LHC for a mass range between 115-126 GeV, and the model is still allowed in a small region for masses between 126-140 GeV.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the mUED parameter region which is excluded by the LHC searches, and we have found that the LHC Higgs boson searches are more sensitive to the mUED model than the direct UED searches.
the mUED is excluded at the 95% C.L. for all values of the fundamental scale M above 1.3 TeV, which is an improvement of about 200 GeV from the previous limit.
we have shown that the Higgs bosons are a powerful tool to constrain UED models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Higgs searches at the LHC are already providing very strong limits on mUED, and that the 8 TeV searches are already providing the strongest limits to date, with the 13 TeV searches expected to be even more powerful.
the Higgs bosons searches at the 7 TeV LHC provide a very strong limit on the mUED parameter region.
the mUED parameter range which was previously allowed by the LHC data is excluded.
